customerJourneyStories.name: Launch and scale a company bike program across countries
customerJourneyStories.summary: Group Mobility and Benefits Director moves from recognizing that a program launch that overwhelms HR, payroll, or procurement teams to repeatedly achieving a repeatable bike-benefit operating model that can be launched country by country with strong employee adoption and low administrative friction through a journey that proves a configurable employer policy model that works across tax and payroll contexts and protects employee adoption across eligible populations.

stages.narrative: The journey starts when Group Mobility and Benefits Director sees that a program launch that overwhelms HR, payroll, or procurement teams is no longer acceptable, or when the current way of working can no longer protect employee adoption across eligible populations.

Group Mobility and Benefits Director discovers the product before active use through benefits brokers, HR communities, employer-benefits platforms, procurement shortlists, peer HR references, and vendor demos. Discovery is the awareness moment, not the task workflow: they connect the offer to "Launch and scale a company bike program across countries" and see credible proof such as a configurable employer policy model that works across tax and payroll contexts.

Group Mobility and Benefits Director evaluates whether the product is right for them after discovery and before trial. They compare employee or operator fit, economic value, administrative effort, service coverage, tax or policy fit, and adoption risk against alternatives, then move to trial only if the evidence shows the product can support "Launch and scale a company bike program across countries", achieve the intended outcome (A repeatable bike-benefit operating model that can be launched country by country with strong employee adoption and low administrative friction), and address the main risk (A program launch that overwhelms HR, payroll, or procurement teams).

The trial succeeds when Group Mobility and Benefits Director can quickly experience design policy and commercial model and connect HR and payroll systems with limited friction and can see early evidence that design, deploy, and run a bike mobility benefit that employees can understand and use while HR, procurement, and payroll can support it without disproportionate manual work will work in the real environment.

Engagement deepens as Group Mobility and Benefits Director uses the product to make open employee enrollment and bike ordering, run the partner network, and measure rollout performance part of normal operations, turning the initial promise into dependable day-to-day value anchored in low-friction enrollment and ordering for employees.

Retention comes when the product keeps making value visible through eligible employee bike adoption, the product still supports the next priority, "Control spend, compliance, and renewal economics", and gives Group Mobility and Benefits Director confidence that staying is safer than switching back or moving elsewhere.

customerJourneyStories.name: Sell, deliver, and activate leased bikes profitably
customerJourneyStories.summary: Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator moves from recognizing that margin erosion from opaque fees or rework to repeatedly achieving a dealer can handle leasing business at scale without sacrificing conversion, margin, or customer satisfaction through a journey that proves structured order intake with fewer missing details and protects qualified leasing demand instead of low-intent traffic.

stages.narrative: The journey starts when Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator sees that margin erosion from opaque fees or rework is no longer acceptable, or when the current way of working can no longer protect qualified leasing demand instead of low-intent traffic.

Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator discovers the product before active use through seller communities, marketplace onboarding pages, partner programs, search results, sales outreach, and peer operator referrals. Discovery is the awareness moment, not the task workflow: they connect the offer to "Sell, deliver, and activate leased bikes profitably" and see credible proof such as structured order intake with fewer missing details.

Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator evaluates whether the product is right for them after discovery and before trial. They compare demand quality, commercial upside, setup effort, operational fit, reporting clarity, trust controls, and support expectations against alternatives, then move to trial only if the evidence shows the product can support "Sell, deliver, and activate leased bikes profitably", achieve the intended outcome (A dealer can handle leasing business at scale without sacrificing conversion, margin, or customer satisfaction), and address the main risk (Margin erosion from opaque fees or rework).

The trial succeeds when Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator can quickly experience receive and validate orders and reserve stock and schedule handover with limited friction and can see early evidence that turn leasing demand into well-prepared orders, efficient handovers, and clean commercial closure will work in the real environment.

Engagement deepens as Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator uses the product to make complete settlement and activation part of normal operations, turning the initial promise into dependable day-to-day value anchored in visibility into expected volume and service demand.

Retention comes when the product keeps making value visible through order completeness rate, the product still supports the next priority, "Run workshop and claims operations with predictable economics", and gives Multi-location Dealer and Service Network Operator confidence that staying is safer than switching back or moving elsewhere.
